about.title: About BMI Calculator
about.description: The BMI Calculator calculates Body Mass Index from height and weight measurements. BMI is a widely used screening reference for underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity categories, but it does not capture all aspects of health or body composition. Use the result as a general reference alongside other health information rather than a standalone medical assessment.

faq.q: What is a healthy BMI range for adults?
faq.a: A healthy BMI typically ranges from 18.5 to 24.9 according to WHO standards. BMI below 18.5 is considered underweight, 25-29.9 is overweight, and 30+ is classified as obese. Our BMI calculator provides these classifications automatically with your results.

faq.q: How should I interpret BMI results?
faq.a: BMI has limitations and may not reflect athletes with high muscle mass, elderly individuals, pregnant women, or some population groups in the same way. It works better as a general screening reference alongside other measures such as body fat percentage and waist circumference.

faq.q: How do I calculate my BMI manually?
faq.a: BMI is calculated using the formula: weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². For imperial units: (weight in pounds ÷ height in inches²) × 703. The calculator automates this process and shows the resulting BMI value with standard reference categories.

faq.q: How often should I check my BMI for health monitoring?
faq.a: For general health monitoring, checking BMI monthly or quarterly is sufficient. If you're actively trying to lose or gain weight, weekly BMI measurements can help track progress alongside other health metrics.

faq.q: What should I do if my BMI is outside the healthy range?
faq.a: If your BMI is outside the standard reference range (18.5-24.9), consider discussing the result with a healthcare provider. They can review your broader health context, body composition, and possible next steps.

faq.q: Can BMI be used for children and teenagers?
faq.a: BMI for children and teenagers is calculated differently using age and sex-specific percentiles rather than adult categories. Our calculator is designed for adults 18+. Consult a pediatrician for child BMI assessments.
